summary: Guidance for safely rolling back combined batching/caching/quantization profile changes after latency and error spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer EchoHealth reported a spike in tail latency and a rise in 5xx stream disconnects following a combined change that: enabled a new quantization profile, increased batching window from 8ms to 25ms, and enabled aggressive KV prefix caching for session replays.

Impact:
- Intermittent p95 latency regressions from ~120ms to 780-1,200ms for certain conversational workloads.
- Increased streaming disconnects (stream_close_rate +3.4%) and transient token generation 5xxs.
- Customers on dedicated pool are seeing increased request timeouts triggering client-side retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: echohealth-prod-gpu-a (us-east region)
- Serving runtime version: 2.9.1+opt (deployed 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC)
- Optimizer profile: hybrid-agg-v2 (batch_window=25ms, kv_prefetch=true, quant=amq8-approx)
- Traffic: 95% chat, 5% embeddings

Steps to reproduce:
1) Route a steady chat workload at production qps to the dedicated pool (we used the customer's canary).
2) Apply optimizer profile hybrid-agg-v2 via the Console rollout (applied to 100% of pool).
3) Observe p95 and streaming error rate over next 15-30 minutes.

Logs / metrics / traces referenced:
- Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/ops/echohealth-latency (p50/p95/p99 timeseries)
- Traces: linked trace ids in investigation notes below
- Recent rollout: Console rollout id ROLLOUT-2026-03-11-752

Customer request:
EchoHealth asked for prescriptive, stepwise guidance to safely revert to the previous stable optimizer configuration with minimal user-visible disruption and no data loss. They requested a temporary protection plan while we investigate root cause.
comments: 2026-03-12 08:04 - Priya Nair: Customer reported symptoms via support form. Attached initial latency dashboard and timeline. Marking as P1 due to production impact.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Liam O'Connor: Acknowledged and starting triage. Asked for full rollout id and whether canary saw similar effects. Requested recording of a sample failing trace.
2026-03-12 09:35 - EchoHealth (Ops contact: Maya Chen): Confirmed canary and full pool had identical symptoms; attached a trace where kv_prefetch shows repeated cache miss thrash.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Liam O'Connor: Ran quick heat-checks: increased batch window correlates with CPU saturation on worker pods and larger micro-batches causing spike in memory pressure when combined with quantized kernels. Hypothesis added to investigation notes.

2026-03-13 02:05 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Prepared hotfix rollback playbook. Will coordinate with customer's on-call for maintenance window if needed. Recommended staged rollback (see investigation notes step sequence).

2026-03-14 06:40 - Liam O'Connor: Executed staged rollback on one AZ; monitoring shows p95 reduced to ~140ms and stream_close_rate back to baseline after KV cache invalidation and quant profile revert on canary nodes. Planning full rollout revert after 1 hour stable period.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Combined effect - quantization profile 'amq8-approx' increases kernel path variability; when paired with larger batch windows the runtime generates larger execution kernels that increase memory working set causing GC/eviction thrash.

Hypothesis B: KV prefix caching with prefetch enabled caused a stampede on cache fill under elevated QPS since batch coalescing altered request ordering, producing hot keys and increased backend IO latency.

Checks performed:
- Node level: top/htop, GPU memory and utilisation, nvtop snapshots during spike windows.
- Runtime logs: looked for 'kv_cache_evict' and 'quant_fallback' messages.
- Telemetry: compared per-token CPU and wall-time distributions pre/post rollout.
- Canary revert: reverted quant profile only on 10% of capacity and observed metrics drop ~60% of the regression within 7 minutes.

Key finding: Reverting quant profile produced the largest immediate improvement on p95. KV cache invalidation helped but only after existing cache fill completed; batch window reduction reduced memory pressure but had slower effect on streaming disconnects.
resolution:
Workaround and rollback plan applied and next steps:
1) Immediate staged revert (already started):
   - Step A (Canary): Revert quant profile on 10% nodes by setting optimizer.quant_profile=baseline-32bit and keep batch_window at 25ms and kv_prefetch=true for observation (done 2026-03-14 06:10 UTC).
   - Monitor p50/p95/stream_close_rate for 30 minutes. If stable, proceed.
   - Step B (AZ staged): Revert quant profile to baseline for an additional 40% (total 50%). After 20 minutes stable, proceed to full pool.
   - Step C (Full): Revert quant profile to baseline for remaining capacity and then address batching/caching changes on a separate maintenance window.
2) KV cache handling: Run coordinated KV cache drain on nodes that had prefetch enabled before toggling caching to avoid stampede (admin command: rwdctl cache invalidate --pool echohealth-prod-gpu-a --mode staged).
3) Batch window rollback (planned): Roll batch_window from 25ms back to 8ms in a separate staged rollout with 5-minute observation windows between stages; prefer a 10% -> 30% -> 100% stage progression.
4) Rollforward vs rollback note: We recommended revert quant first because it yielded largest effect; batching and caching to be handled after the quant change to avoid overlapping effects.
5) Postmortem actions: Create a canary test harness for hybrid profiles and add an automated alert if p95 increases >2x within 10 minutes of optimizer profile change.

Follow-up items assigned:
- Engineering (optimizer): add conservative fallback for 'amq8-approx' that disables prefetch when batch_window > 20ms (PR requested: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimizer/pull/5018).
- SRE: add dashboard panel that correlates batch_window, kv_prefetch, and quant profile usage with p95 and stream_close_rate.
- Support: produce a short runbook for customers introducing hybrid optimizer profiles with recommended rollout percentages and observation windows.

Status: Canary revert successful; full rollback in progress. Will update when full pool reversion completes and when follow-up PR merges.
